chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Decline of the big bands
summary: McRae says the big bands began to lose the crowds as promoters oversold, the Depression bit and musicians tired of travel.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: If you were in a band like Chick Webb's,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
that was your job. If you was in a band like Cab (inaudible), that was your job.
As long as you played the man's music, that's what you were supposed to do.
And this was a great year, I'd say. One of the greatest year for music -- the big bands with music -- until then we get into the small bands.
Even when Louie Jordan left us and went into the small band -- they started getting into that small band area -- that was a great year for --
Because you must remember, that was still during the Depression and money was really getting tighter.
Then the crowds began to fall off, you know -- the big bands. You know, the promoters were overdoing it.
They were putting too many attractions on the road. People were squawking about too many bands are coming in, you know.
Then the musicians got tired. A lot of them didn't want to travel.
